audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart is shifted out of step with its own reasons in the first four rows: Level 1 was marked Aurora while whys[0] says Jax trades autos ahead of her; Level 2 was Skill while whys[1] says she owns the spacing; Level 3 was Jax while whys[2] calls it 'genuinely a skill window'; Levels 4-5 was Jax while whys[3] says the gap keeps her safe.
audit.why: The packet levelChart and the mirror audit agree: Jax / Aurora / Skill / Aurora / Aurora / Jax / Jax. Jax owns level 1 and everything from first item; she owns 2 and 4-6.
audit.corrected: Level 1 Jax, Level 2 Aurora, Level 3 Skill, Levels 4-6 Aurora, first item and two items Jax.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4].why and breakdown.late call Jax's ult 'Grandmaster’s Might', and the Level 6 row does not name her actual spike.
audit.why: The content layer and mirror both use Grandmaster at Arms. Her Level 6 threat is Between Worlds (140s at rank 1), which slows and lets her teleport across the zone — a far longer cooldown than Jax's 110s R, so the ult race is winnable if she spends hers first.
audit.corrected: Grandmaster at Arms (110s at rank 1) versus Between Worlds (140s at rank 1). Jax's spikes: level 1, first item, two items. Hers: level 2 spacing, and 6.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer names Twofold Hex as 'her escape' in the cooldown block, dosFull[0], report[5] and the loading screen. Twofold Hex is her Q — a 900-range poke missile that recasts to drag the curse back. Her escape is Across the Veil (W, 22s at rank 1).
audit.why: Tracking the wrong cooldown produces the wrong engage timing: a player waits out a 9s Q instead of the 22s blink that actually denies Leap Strike.
audit.corrected: Track Across the Veil (22s at rank 1) — that is what resets the gap. Counter Strike dodges attacks only, so Twofold Hex, its recast pull, The Weirding and Between Worlds all land on a Jax standing in E; she throws few autos, so hold E for her commit, not her poke.

audit.whatIsWrong: The three flagged suspectNames are false positives.
audit.why: 'Hold Counter Strike', 'Use Leap Strike' and 'Counter Strike-stun' are all real Jax names with a verb attached. The packet's other defect — that the page never names Aurora's abilities — was true of the full layer only; the content layer names Twofold Hex.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Twofold Hex's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: If she ranks poke and refuses melee, the gap keeps her safe while Twofold Hex chips and your stun has no autos to dodge.

edits.before: Grandmaster’s Might stats win every extended duel from here on. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Aurora's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: A full spirit-stack root into burst can kill you before Grandmaster at Arms' Armor and MR land — don't all-in her combo.

edits.before: Trinity Force is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Twofold Hex's cooldown.
edits.after: Trinity Force plus your R flips it — stick through one blink and out-duel her squishy AP body.

edits.after: Two items on: Leap Strike sticks, Counter Strike stuns, and R's resists eat her burst — no skirmish-mage out-duels you.

notes: Both layers had the chart shifted a row out of step with the packet and the mirror; the four moved rows are proposed as full/content pairs in one atomic group. The full layer's central error was calling Twofold Hex 'her escape' — it is her 900-range Q poke; Across the Veil (W, 22s) is the blink, and that is the cooldown a Jax must bait. Content layer was already accurate and mostly left alone.
